description: Remote unauthenticated HTTP/2 heap-buffer-overflow in session.altsvc() with a long origin - github.com/nodejs/node
overview: A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt process memory. When an application passes an attacker-controlled value such as a request's `:authority` header to `Http2Session.altsvc()`, the AltSvc implementation in `src/node_http2.cc` allocates a buffer sized to the origin length and then writes it with a null terminator, placing one byte past the end of the allocation. A single request carrying a long but syntactically valid `:authority` triggers the out-of-bounds write, which aborts the process and serves as a remote heap-corruption primitive. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.
